_source: Available water capacity (mm of water per metre of soil) from the midpoints of FAO-56 Table 19 ranges, with typical values for common Indian soil groups.

sandy.name: Sandy
sandy.tip: Sandy soil drains fast and holds little water. Irrigate lightly and more often, and add organic matter to improve water holding.

sandy_loam.name: Sandy loam
sandy_loam.tip: Sandy loam drains well. Moderate, regular irrigation works best; avoid heavy single irrigations that leach nutrients.

loamy.name: Loamy
loamy.tip: Loamy soil holds water well and drains well. Standard irrigation intervals usually work.

alluvial.name: Alluvial
alluvial.tip: Alluvial soils of the Indo-Gangetic plains hold water well. Level the field so irrigation water spreads evenly.

silty.name: Silty / silt loam
silty.tip: Silty soil holds a lot of water but can form a surface crust. Avoid flooding and break crusts after irrigation.

clay_loam.name: Clay loam
clay_loam.tip: Clay loam holds water for a long time. Allow longer intervals between irrigations and ensure drainage.

clay.name: Clay
clay.tip: Clay soil absorbs water slowly and can waterlog. Apply water slowly, avoid over-irrigation and keep drainage channels open.

black.name: Black (Regur)
black.tip: Black cotton soil holds a lot of water and cracks when dry. Irrigate before deep cracks form and avoid waterlogging.

red.name: Red
red.tip: Red soil is porous with low water holding. Irrigate more frequently and add compost or farmyard manure.

laterite.name: Laterite
laterite.tip: Laterite soil drains quickly and is low in nutrients. Mulching and organic matter help keep moisture.
